summary: Make pressure differences and the pressure-force origin of upthrust easier to see and practise.

improvements.where: note, after the hydrostatic-pressure paragraph in ## Key ideas
improvements.why: Outcome 9702-4.3.4 requires using a pressure difference between depths; the chapter has no diagram, and students can confuse the difference with total pressure.
improvements.what: graph_sketch of pressure p against vertical depth h in a uniform stationary liquid open to air: straight line with positive slope, intercept labelled $p_{\mathrm{atm}}$, two depths $h_1$ and $h_2$ with pressure rise $\Delta p=\rho g(h_2-h_1)$. Explain that the slope is $\rho g$ and the intercept is the surface pressure.

improvements.where: note, after the upthrust paragraph in ## Key ideas
improvements.why: The note states $U=(p_b-p_t)A$ and $U=\rho gV_{\mathrm{displaced}}$ separately but skips the algebra that joins them; this is central to outcomes 9702-4.3.5 and 9702-4.3.6.
improvements.what: Add a compact derivation for a fully immersed vertical prism: $p_b-p_t=\rho_{\mathrm{fluid}}g\Delta h$, so $U=(p_b-p_t)A=\rho_{\mathrm{fluid}}gA\Delta h=\rho_{\mathrm{fluid}}gV_{\mathrm{displaced}}$. State that equal displaced volumes in the same fluid have equal upthrust even at different depths, while individual surface pressure forces change.

improvements.why: Outcome 9702-4.3.3 has only five tagged items, and the examiner reports show confusion between pressure difference, upthrust and resultant force.
improvements.what: One structured Show (that) item linking $m=\rho A\Delta h$, weight and $\Delta p=F/A$ with all intermediate steps; one Explain item comparing equal-volume fully immersed blocks at different depths and distinguishing the pressure forces from their difference. Use only additive items with full hints and explanations.
